speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you have been experiencing chronic joint pain; to help me narrow this down, how would you describe the location of the pain and has it been present for more than six weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis (secondary to gout or prior trauma). The patient is a 69-year-old male with chronic pain in the left great toe, hips, and knees, worsening with activity and improving with rest. This pattern is most consistent with osteoarthritis, but I will confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: X-RAY of left foot, hips, and knees.

REQUEST IMAGES: Left great toe, hips, and knees X-rays.
